title: French Onion Filet Mignon
ingredients:
Filet mignon
2 yellow or sweet onions
Butter
Vegetable or olive oil
Salt
Black pepper
Beef broth
Gruyère cheese
Worcestershire sauce
Garlic
Thyme
instructions:
Cut the onions into thin slices.
Cook the onions: Put 1 tablespoon butter + a small spoonful of oil in a large pan over medium-low heat. Add onions.
Caramelize: Cook the onions for about 25–40 minutes, stirring every few minutes. You want them soft and golden brown, not black.
Make the French onion broth: Add about 1 cup beef broth to the onions, plus a little Worcestershire sauce, garlic, and thyme. Let it gently cook for about 5 minutes.
Prepare the filet: Season both sides generously with salt + pepper.
Sear: Put a little oil in a pan over medium-high heat. Cook the filet for about 2–3 minutes on each side to brown it.
Add the French onion topping: Put the filets in an oven-safe pan/dish. Spoon some caramelized onions over each steak.
Add Gruyère: Put Gruyère cheese over the onions.
Finish in the oven: Put them in a 425°F oven until the steak reaches the temperature you want. Use your thermometer instead of relying only on time. For medium-rare, aim around 130–135°F after resting; for medium, around 140–145°F.
Serve: Put some of your French onion broth in a shallow bowl, then place the filet with the onions and melted Gruyère into the broth.
